terms.why: 'Anh hùng' is the heroic register; 'người hùng' reads as a news headline about a rescue.
'Bùng nổ' carries the explosive, everything-clicks sense. A bare 'Vùng' would just mean 'area'.
One syllable, and it keeps the meter-filling metaphor the English has.
The standard word for a sudden, irreversible awakening — exactly the one-off moment this is.
Two syllables. 'Điểm huấn luyện' is correct and far too long for the labels that carry it.
CLB is the everyday abbreviation for câu lạc bộ, and every Vietnamese football fan reads it instantly.
The pull a club has on the town's attention — what the meter is actually measuring.
The established comic-book term. Case is not locked: it is a common noun in both languages.
The ordinary word for a club being known. "Uy tín" is closer to trustworthiness, and it had drifted into three strings.
